attributes.composition: consisted mainly of Nb and Mo

evidence.quote: The precipitates inside the bcc phase had the B2 structure, while the B2 matrix contained the bcc precipitates. EDS maps (Fig. 2 c) showed that the bcc precipitates consisted mainly of Nb and Mo almost without of Co and Hf.

In turn, the B2 particles in the bcc phase were (Co, Hf)-rich (Fig. 2 d). The size and volume fraction of the bcc precipitates in the B2 matrix were 12 nm and 30%, respectively. The B2 precipitates in the bcc phase were mostly finer and had the mean size of ~4 nm. However, some much coarser B2 precipitates with the size of ~70 nm were also found (Fig. 2 d).

A closer look at the microstructure revealed the presence of nanoscale bcc precipitates inside the B2 phase, and, vice versa, the B2 precipitates within the bcc phase (Fig. 3 b). The estimated size of the bcc / B2 precipitates was 15 / 6 nm, respectively.

evidence.quote: The (HfCo)90(NbMo)10 alloy comprised the B2 matrix grains and bcc / B2 eutectic regions. The volume ratio between the B2 and bcc phases was ≈ 8:1. In addition, a small amount (2%) of the Nb-rich bcc phase, located usually at B2 grains/ eutectic regions interfaces, was found.

evidence.quote: The (HfCo)75(NbMo)25 had mostly the bcc + B2 eutectic structure with some primary bcc particles. In this alloy, some nanoscale bcc / B2 precipitates were detected inside the B2 / bcc phases, respectively. The B2 / bcc ratio was ≈ 7:3; some Nb-rich bcc particles were also detected.

evidence.quote: A closer look at the microstructure revealed the presence of nanoscale bcc precipitates inside the B2 phase, and, vice versa, the B2 precipitates within the bcc phase (Fig. 3 b). The estimated size of the bcc / B2 precipitates was 15 / 6 nm, respectively. Again, similarly to the (HfCo)90(NbMo)10 alloy, some coarser (~70 nm) B2 nanoprecipitates were found in the Nb-rich bcc phase (Fig. 3 d).

Annealing did not result in the formation of additional phases, which agreed with the Thermo-Calc predictions. However, annealing led to the formation of (i) B2 / bcc nanoprecipitates inside the initial bcc / B2 phases and (ii) separate Nb-rich and Mo-rich bcc phases.
the room-temperature yield strength of the (HfCo)90(NbMo)10 alloy increased from 640 to 1340 MPa.

Hardening was induced by the bcc nanoprecipitates in the B2 phase according to the Orowan mechanism.

In the (HfCo)75(NbMo)25 alloy, the strengthening effect of annealing was smaller compared to the (HfCo)90(NbMo)10 alloy since the precipitates were presented already in the as-cast state [23], and the annealing only increased their fraction.
It can be hypothesized that an addition of Co and/or Hf limits the mutual solubility of Nb and Mo, yet future work is required to verify this assumption.
